payload.prompt: We sent an invoice for 1791 EUR to Silveroak Ltd (org no. 906661551) when the exchange rate was 11.03 NOK/EUR. The customer has now paid, but the rate is 10.66 NOK/EUR. Register the payment and post the exchange rate difference (disagio) to the correct account.

payload.goal: Register customer payment for an EUR invoice to Silveroak Ltd and post the exchange rate loss (disagio) caused by payment at a lower NOK/EUR rate than invoicing.
likely_resources: ledger accounts for exchange rate gain/loss
success_checks: Customer Silveroak Ltd with org no. 906661551 exists
Invoice for 1791 EUR is created/found and linked to the customer
Payment is registered against the invoice in EUR
Booked NOK value at invoice rate and payment rate is reflected correctly
Exchange rate difference is posted as a loss/disagio to the correct ledger account
Invoice balance is fully closed after payment and currency adjustment

Invoice date and payment date are not provided; exact dates may be required for posting
No invoice number is provided, so matching the correct invoice may require lookup or creation

It is not explicit whether 1791 EUR is gross or net, but for payment registration the original invoice total is the key amount

payload.suggested_first_action: Create or locate customer Silveroak Ltd and the EUR invoice for 1791 EUR before registering the payment.
ordered_steps: Create or verify bank account setup for payment registration
Create or verify customer Silveroak Ltd with organization number 906661551
Create or locate the customer invoice in EUR for total 1791 if it does not already exist in the empty sandbox
Ensure the invoice is posted using exchange rate 11.03 NOK/EUR
Register incoming payment on the invoice using exchange rate 10.66 NOK/EUR
Calculate exchange rate difference as NOK booked at invoice rate minus NOK received at payment rate
Post the resulting negative currency difference as disagio to the configured exchange rate loss account via voucher if not auto-posted
Verify the invoice is fully settled and the ledger contains the exchange rate loss posting

payload.headline: Rate limit hit before payment registration; invoice created but payment+disagio not posted.
what_went_wrong: LLM rate limit (429) hit exactly when trying to call PUT /invoice/{id}/:payment, leaving the payment unregistered and disagio unposted.
Invoice was booked at Tripletex's live rate (~11.295 NOK/EUR) instead of the required 11.03 NOK/EUR, meaning the disagio calculation will differ from expected.
Two parallel GET /ledger/account calls were made (one before and one after invoice creation), wasting tokens and contributing to the rate limit breach.
The payment PUT call was attempted without query parameters being shown in the trace, suggesting the call may have been malformed even before the rate limit error.
what_worked: Customer, order, order line, and invoice were all created successfully in EUR with correct amount (1791 EUR).
Correct accounts identified: 8160 Valutatap (disagio) id=466213725 and payment type id=36705431.
what_to_try_next: Retry the PUT /invoice/{id}/:payment with explicit query params: paymentTypeId=36705431, paymentDate, paidAmount (NOK at 10.66 rate), paidAmountCurrency=1791.00, and verify disagio is auto-posted.
Reduce redundant API calls (e.g. duplicate GET /ledger/account) to stay under token rate limits and free up budget for the critical payment step.
Investigate whether Tripletex allows setting a custom exchange rate at invoice creation time (e.g. via currency rate override) so the booked NOK amount matches the 11.03 rate specified in the task.
unnecessary_calls: Second GET /ledger/account after invoice creation — duplicate of the first call made before order creation.
GET /invoice/2147612638 immediately after POST /invoice — the POST response already contains invoice details including amounts.
